title: Flapping fallback behavior and KV-cache warmup causing EU SLO blip
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Incident where EU region experienced a 99th-percentile latency SLO breach and elevated error rates for ~27 minutes due to repeated fallback flapping between EU-primary and secondary regions, coupled with cold KV-cache misses after failover. This ticket captures timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and tracked follow-up action items.
impact_summary: From 2026-03-10T10:12 to 2026-03-10T10:39 UTC, EU traffic saw 99p latency spike from 180ms to 1.2s and error rate rose to 4.3%. Customer-facing degradation: chat completions truncated or delayed; API error rate exceeded SLO for 27 minutes. Rough estimated affected requests: ~42k. No data loss.
root_cause: A sequence of interacting issues: (1) Circuit-breaker hysteresis thresholds on the edge router were misaligned with control-plane health checks, causing rapid fallback toggles when a transient GPU scheduler delay occurred. (2) Failovers routed traffic to a cold pool where KV-cache warmup TTLs had expired and pre-warm tasks were throttled by autoscaler handoff. (3) Load-shedding policy prioritized bulk token-limited requests incorrectly, dropping small interactive requests first, worsening tail latency. The combined effect amplified tail latency and triggered further flapping.
timeline: 10:10 UTC: Minor scheduler backpressure in eu-west-1 due to concurrent large-batch jobs — latency began to rise slowly
10:12 UTC: Edge CBs tripped on EU nodes due to increased p99; automated fallback to EU-secondary (eu-central) began
10:15 UTC: Control plane health probe latency briefly exceeded threshold; some nodes marked unhealthy and removed from pool
10:16-10:23 UTC: Repeated oscillation: traffic shunted between primary and secondary regions with CB reopen/close cycles (~3-5s hysteresis mismatch)
10:18 UTC: Autoscaler initiated additional nodes in eu-central but new nodes entered service without warmed KV-caches
10:20 UTC: Load-shedding policy dropped interactive requests due to mis-prioritization; tails spiked further
10:30 UTC: On-call manually increased hysteresis and pinned routing to eu-central to stabilize traffic
10:35 UTC: Pre-warm script executed across new nodes, KV-cache hitrate recovered to baseline
10:39 UTC: Latency/error metrics returned to within SLOs; incident declared mitigated
Post-incident: 10:40-12:00 UTC: Monitoring and synthetic checks validated stability
immediate_mitigation: Raised circuit-breaker hysteresis windows by +5s on edge routers serving EU to prevent flip-flopping (manual roll) — owner: Liam Chen — completed 10:30 UTC
Pinned routing to eu-central for 25 minutes to prevent thrash while autoscaler finished warmup — owner: On-call — completed 10:31 UTC
Triggered KV-cache pre-warm for newly provisioned nodes and temporarily increased pre-warm concurrency — owner: SRE — completed 10:35 UTC
Adjusted load-shedding priority temporarily to prefer keeping interactive requests (small token requests) — owner: Platform Ops — completed 10:22 UTC
long_term_action_items: Align edge CB hysteresis config with control-plane health-check cadence and add automated config drift alerts — owner: Liam Chen — due: 2026-04-02
Implement a KV-cache pre-warm handshake during autoscaler handoff so instances register as 'ready' only after cache warmup completes — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-04-09
Rework load-shedding policy to include request shape (interactive vs bulk) and add unit+integration tests to prevent regressions — owner: Marco Alvarez — due: 2026-03-28
Create synthetic multi-region failover exercise runbook and schedule quarterly game days to validate hysteresis and autoscaler interactions — owner: Reliability Eng Team — due: 2026-05-01
Add a dashboard that correlates CB open/close events, KV-cache hit rate, and autoscaler events for faster triage — owner: Observability — due: 2026-03-24
Introduce a canary gate that verifies KV-cache hit rate > 85% before shifting production traffic during autoscale-based rollouts — owner: Runtime Eng — due: 2026-04-15
postmortem_notes: This incident is a classic emergent behavior case where independent safety mechanisms (CBs, autoscaler, cache warmers, load-shedding) interacted in untested ways. We observed that individual subsystems behaved within their design parameters but their interactions produced a harmful feedback loop. The next steps focus on shrinking the blast radius of each subsystem during transitions and building cross-system integration tests.
